ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r3.claim: Pharaoh repeatedly promised to accept Moses's demand if calamities were lifted, then broke his word, increasing Moses's influence among the Copts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p161/r3.anchor: repeated breaches were instrumental in increasing the influence of Moses (sws) on the Copts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r1.claim: In Pharaoh's expanded speech, he boasts of Egypt's sovereignty and rivers and disparages Moses before his people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r1.anchor: Do not the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers which flow beneath my feet belong to me?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r2.claim: Pharaoh's speech also asks why gold ornaments or angels did not accompany Moses; it befools his disobedient people before God drowns them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r2.anchor: He was able to befool his people through this speech and they were in fact a people disobedient

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God invited even Pharaoh to repentance; no one may make people despair of it, and repentance begins with God's enabling turn toward the servant.
DURR-FULL:v4p315/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: دعا الله إلى توبته من قال (أنا ربكم الأعلى)

DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.claim: Gabriel recounts that Pharaoh had claimed divinity, then stuffed his mouth when drowning threatened, fearing he would receive mercy.
DURR-FULL:v4p387/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قال لي جبريل: ما غضب ربك على أحد

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r3.claim: This telling explains gentle speech and condenses Pharaoh's deepest tyranny into his claim to be the highest lord.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r3.anchor: Buradaki hususiyeti ise kavl-i leyyini îzah ve Firavun’un أَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ tuğyânıyla Firavunluğunun künhünü hulâsa etmiş olmasıdır.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r22.claim: Pharaoh claimed to be the highest among lords, placing himself above every other lord and demanding worship under that title.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r22.anchor: Kendisinden başka herhangi bir rabbi kendi mâdûnunda addederek kendisinin en üstün rabbü’lerbâb olduğunu iddia etmek derecesinde davayı azıttı

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r23.claim: Pharaoh had earlier claimed not to know any god except himself in al-Qaṣaṣ and threatened Moses over taking another god in al-Shuʿarāʾ.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r23.anchor: Daha evvel Sûre-i Kasas’ta مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى [28/38] demişti, Sûre-i Şu‘arâ’da[^5] da لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى [26/29] demişti.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r24.claim: The inquiry he staged by ordering Hāmān to build a tower was not fruitless: Pharaoh tacitly acknowledged a god existed but claimed that god was not above him.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r24.anchor: bir rab bulunduğunu anlamış[^9] olduğunu îmâ etmekle beraber onun kendinden yüksek olmadığını iddia edecek derecede kibr ü azamet taslamaya kalkmıştı.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r25.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r25.claim: Ibn Jarīr transmits from Mujāhid and others that forty years separated Pharaoh's two claims.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r25.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in Mücâhid ve sâireden nakline göre bu iki söz arasında kırk sene geçmişti.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r26.claim: An account recorded by al-Ālūsī says Pharaoh rose before his assembled people, delivered a speech, and uttered his boast as their ruler.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r26.anchor: Âlûsî’nin kaydettiği vechile bazı âsârda şöyle vârid olmuştur ki Firavun topladığı mahşeri içinde kalkıp hitabetle bir nutuk îrâd ederek o büyük lakırdıyı söylemiş

ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n10/r1.claim: Pharaoh's claim to divine status is his cardinal sin and the transgression of right; Asad cross-references 28:38 and its note 36.
ASAD-NOTES:79:20#n10/r1.anchor: Pharaoh's claim to divine status is the cardinal sin whereby "he has transgressed all bounds of what is right" (verse 17 above).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r7.claim: Pharaoh persisted in unbelief and rebellion, assembled the magicians and his men, and declared himself divine.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r7.anchor: inkâr ve isyandan vazgeçmediği gibi sihirbazları ve adamlarını toplayıp onlara “Ben sizin en yüce rabbinizim!” diyerek kendi tanrılığını ilân etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r8.claim: Pharaoh’s boast illustrates how far ambition for rank and status and self-assertion can go.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r8.anchor: Firavun’un, “Ben sizin en yüce rabbinizim” şeklindeki iddiası, insandaki makam ve mevki tutkusunun, benlik iddiasının nerelere kadar varabileceğini gösteren ibretlik bir sözdür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r9.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r9.claim: Ghazālī says the impulse behind Pharaoh’s claim exists within every person, though some reveal it while others restrain or suppress it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r9.anchor: Firavun’a, “Ben sizin en büyük tanrınızım” dedirten motif aslında her insanın içinde saklıdır; fakat kimi bunu dışarı vurur, kimi de bazı sebeplerle içinde tutar veya bastırır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r10.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r10.claim: Ghazālī describes this arrogance as a distorted form of every person’s desire for perfection, elevation, and liberation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r10.anchor: her insanda bulunan yetkinlik, yükselme ve özgürleşme arzusu ve arayışının saptırılmış şeklidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r11.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r11.claim: Ghazālī says true perfection, elevation, and freedom come only through turning to God, knowing Him, obeying His will, and adopting divine character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r11.anchor: gerçek yetkinliğe, yükselme ve özgürleşmeye ancak ve ancak Allah’a yönelmek, O’nu tanımak (mârifet), buyruğuna ve rızâsına göre yaşamak, ilâhî ahlâk ile bezenmekle ulaşılabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r12.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r12.claim: Ghazālī regards other claims to selfhood and perfection as misery and decline.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:15/r12.anchor: Bunun dışındaki bütün benlik ve yetkinlik iddiaları tam tersine gerçekte bir sefalettir, düşüştür

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#4/r1.speaker: خيثمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#4/r1.claim: Khaythama says forty years separated Pharaoh’s claim that he knew no god for them besides himself from his claim to be their highest lord.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p346#4/r1.anchor: عن خيثمة قال كان بين قول فرعون ﴿ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ﴾ وبين قوله ﴿ أنا ربكم الأعلى ﴾ أربعون سنة

BURSEVI:v10p250/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r9.claim: His declaration means that he claimed there was no lord above him.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r9.anchor: {فقال} لقيامة مقام الحكومة والسلطنة {أنا ربكم الاعلى} لا رب فوقي

BURSEVI:v10p250/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r10.claim: The superlative can refer to his rank over the kings and officials under his rule.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r10.anchor: على أن تكون صيغة التفضيل بالنسبة إلى من كان تحت ولايته من الملوك والأمراء

BURSEVI:v10p250/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r11.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p250/r11.claim: Al-Kāshifī interprets Pharaoh as saying that the idols resembling him were all gods and that he was higher than them.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r11.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : يعني أصنام كه بر صورت منند

BURSEVI:v10p250/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r12.claim: After the sorcerers were defeated, Moses was told that he was the higher one, since victory over the magic was victory over Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r12.anchor: قيل لموسى عليه السلام في مقابلة هذا الكلام إنك أنت الأعلى لأن الغلبة على سحره غلبة عليه

BURSEVI:v10p250/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r13.claim: Pharaoh was not claiming to have created the heavens, earth, mountains, plants, or animals; that claim would be self-evidently false.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r13.anchor: لم يرد بهذا القول إنه خالق السموات والأرض والجبال والنبات والحيوان

BURSEVI:v10p250/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r14.claim: Anyone who doubts that created things have a creator is insane; an insane person could not have been sent a messenger by God.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r14.anchor: ومن شك فيه كان مجنونا ولو كان مجنونا لما جاز من الله بعثة الرسول إليه

BURSEVI:v10p250/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p250/r15.claim: Rather, Pharaoh was a materialist who denied the Creator and resurrection, claiming that he alone nurtured and benefited his people.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r15.anchor: بل الرجل كان دهريا منكرا للصانع والحشر والنشر

BURSEVI:v10p250/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r16.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p250/r16.claim: One view says that after his humiliation and helplessness before the transformed staff, Pharaoh should not have made the claim; he seemed delirious and unaware of his words.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r16.anchor: قال بعضهم : كان ينبغي له عند ظهور ذله وعجزه بانقلاب العصا حية إن لا يقول ذلك القول

BURSEVI:v10p250/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p250/r17.speaker: الإمام القشيري
BURSEVI:v10p250/r17.claim: Al-Qushayrī relates that Iblīs could not bear Pharaoh's boast: Iblīs had claimed good for himself and suffered calamity, so he wondered what would befall Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v10p250/r17.anchor: (إمام قشيري رحمه الله) : در لطائف آورده كه إبليس اين سخن شنيده كفت مراطاقت اين سخن نيست

QASHANI:79:18-26/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r5.claim: He pursued satanic schemes and psychical tricks against Moses, was expelled from the holy presence, and his veil grew.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r5.anchor: يسعى } في دفع موسى بالمكايد الشيطانية والحيل النفسانية فرد عن جناب القدس مطرودا وازداد حجابه

QASHANI:79:18-26/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r6.claim: His claim to be the highest lord contests divine majesty; he was subdued and cast into the Fire, like one who contests God’s grandeur and pride.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r6.anchor: أنا ربكم الأعلى } أو نازع الحق لشدة ظهور أنائيته رداء الكبرياء فقهر وقذف في النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r1.claim: Under the second parsing, an implied يقول is supplied: Pharaoh is saying, “I am your highest lord,” with the additional figurative usage this requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r1.anchor: وعلى الثاني فيه تقدير أي فقال يقول فرعون أنا ربكم الخ مع ما في الثاني من التجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r2.claim: A report says Pharaoh stood addressing his people and uttered that outrageous claim to elevate himself above all who administered their affairs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p30#4/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنه قام فيهم خطيبا فقال تلك العظيمة وأراد اللعين تفضيل نفسه على كل من يلي أمورهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r3.claim: Pharaoh's claim means there is no lord above him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that Pharaoh claimed to be lord over his idols, which he called lords.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد أن الأصنام أرباب وأنا ربكم وربها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r2.claim: Pharaoh's boast means he claimed to be supreme over everyone who managed his affairs.

BINTSHATI:v1p147/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p147/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p147/r8.claim: The three-word proclamation is too terse to be a formal address; its brevity conveys the tyrant’s alarm and matches the surah’s decisive pace.
BINTSHATI:v1p147/r8.anchor: والإيجاز البليغ في قوله: {أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَى} ينفي أن يكون الموقف موقف خطابه، وإنما هي كلمات ثلاث لم تزد.

BINTSHATI:v1p148/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r2.claim: Al-aʿla here is absolute and unrestricted, not a comparative meaning “higher than another”; the author compares its form with superlatives in al-Layl.
BINTSHATI:v1p148/r2.anchor: فليس القصد منه معنى المفاضلة، وإنما هو الإطلاق غير المحدود بمفضول، ومثله: الأشقى، والأتقى، والأعلى ف سورة الليل،

SULAMI:v2p370#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p370#5/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p370#5/r1.claim: Asked why God created and manifested sins and words unsuited to lordship, Wāsiṭī answers that attributes appearing in originated things do not affect the divine Essence, which transcends even verbal description.
SULAMI:v2p370#5/r1.anchor: سئل الواسطي : لماذا خلق الله المعاصي وأظهرها واظهر هذه الألفاظ التي لا تليق بالربوبية ؟ قال : لأنه لم يؤثر على الذات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r9.speaker: حمزة الكرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r9.claim: Hamza al-Kirmani reports that Moses promised Pharaoh four hundred years of joy and then Paradise if he believed, but Haman dissuaded him from becoming a servant after being worshiped as lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r9.anchor: وقال حمزة الكرماني : قال له موسى عليه السلام : إن ربي أرسلني إليك , لئن آمنت بربك تكون أربعمائة سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r10.claim: The author takes Pharaoh's proclamation as claiming that people are lords ranked over one another and that he is the highest, with none above him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r10.anchor: يعني كلكم أرباب بعضكم فوق بعض وأنا أعلاكم , ولا رب فوقي أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r11.claim: Pharaoh's premise was that divinity is nature apportioned among beings, with the highest being most capable of obtaining what is desired.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r11.anchor: وذلك لأن الإله عنده الطبيعة , وهي مقسمة في الموجودات , فهم كلهم أرباب , ومن كان أعلى كان أقعد في المراد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r12.claim: The author curses Ibn ʿArabi, Ibn al-Fāriḍ, and their followers for denying the sovereign God, and places al-Ḥallāj after Pharaoh in this error.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p315/r12.anchor: ولعن من تمذهب بمذهبه كابن عربي وابن الفارض وأتباعهما حيث أنكروا المختار الملك ثم الحلاج بعد فرعون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r1.claim: Among Pharaoh’s many clear signs and proofs, al-Biqāʿī calls self-evident productive inference the greatest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الآيات البينات والدلائل الواضحات التي لا تحصى وهي كثيرة , وأعظمها القياس البديهي الإنتاج

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r2.speaker: إبليس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r2.claim: A report says Satan wondered that Pharaoh made the lordship claim after Satan himself suffered for pride against Adam.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r2.anchor: ويروى أن إبليس لما سمع منه قوله هذا قال : إني تجبرت على آدم قلقيت ما لقيت , وهذا يقول هذا ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r3.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r3.claim: Al-Ghazālī says obedience is difficult because the soul recoils from servitude and craves lordship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r3.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي في كتاب الصبر من الإحياء : فالصبر على الطاعة شديد لأن النفس بطبعها تنفر عن العبودية وتشتهي الربوبية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r4.claim: A gnostic says every soul inwardly harbors Pharaoh’s claim, though only Pharaoh found the opportunity and acceptance to voice it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r4.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : ما من نفس إلا وهي مضمرة ما أظهره فرعون من قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r5.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r5.claim: The gnostic says people implicitly claim lordship over servants and subordinates; resentment at their service signals hidden pride contesting God’s majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r5.anchor: فإن امتعاضه وغيظه عند تقصيرهم في خدمته لا يصدر إلا عن إضمار الكبر ومنازعة الربوبية في رداء الكبرياء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r6.claim: Al-Biqāʿī adduces that the Prophet never reproached a servant as support for the gnostic’s point.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p316/r6.anchor: ويؤيده أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما لام خادمه في شيء قط

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses tempted Pharaoh with renewed youth, secure kingship, restored pleasures, and Paradise if he believed; after Haman dissuaded him, Pharaoh declared himself the highest lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى قال : قال موسى : يا فرعون هل لك في ان اعطيك شبابك لا تهرم ، وملكك لا ينزع منك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr says forty years separated the two statements mentioned in the surrounding passage.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3398#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال : بين كلمتين اربعون سنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r9.claim: The فاء in “then he called” conveys that Pharaoh proclaimed his statement as soon as the people arrived, from eagerness to deliver it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r9.anchor: وعطف { فنادى } بالفاء لإفادة أنه أعلن هذا القول لهم بفور حضورهم لفرط حرصه على إبلاغ ذلك إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r10.claim: Calling literally means raising one’s voice to summon someone; vocative particles stand for “I call,” so the following noun is accusative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r10.anchor: والنداء : حقيقته جهر الصوت بدعوة أحد ليحضر ولذلك كانت حروف النداء نائبة مناب ( أدعو ) فنصبت الاسم الواقع بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r11.claim: Calling can also mean merely raising the voice by necessary association; al-Ḥarīrī’s repeated “call” in the thirtieth Maqāma illustrates this usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r11.anchor: ويطلق النداء على رفع الصوت دون طلب حضور مجازا مرسلا بعلاقة اللزوم كقول الحريري في ( المقامة الثلاثين ) ( فحين جلس كأنه ابن ماء السماء ، نادى مناد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r12.claim: As with “he gathered,” the object of “he called out” is omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p79/r12.anchor: وحذف مفعول ( نادى ) كما حذف مفعول ( حشر )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r1.claim: Attributing the gathering and call to Pharaoh is figurative: his followers and soldiers carried them out at his command, as people say al-Manṣūr built Baghdad.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r1.anchor: وإسناد الحشر والنداء إلى فرعون مجاز عقلي لأنه لا يباشر بنفسه حشر الناس ولا نداءهم ولكن يأمر أتباعه وجنده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r2.claim: Pharaoh recalled his people’s belief that Egypt’s king was divine because priests claimed he was Amun-Ra’s son, with the sun as that god’s manifestation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r2.anchor: والقول الذي نادى به هو تذكير قومه بمعتقدهم فيه فإنهم كانوا يعتبرون ملك مصر إلاها لأن الكهنة يخبرونهم بأنه ابن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r3.claim: The restrictive form “I am your lord” counters Moses’ call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r3.anchor: وصيغة الحصر في { أنا ربكم } لرد دعوة موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r4.claim: “He said, ‘I am your highest lord’” appositively restates the call; repeating the conjunction with the governing clause can emphasize an apposition, as in the cited Qur’anic example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r4.anchor: بدلا مطابقا بإعادة حرف العطف ، وهو الفاء لأن البدل قد يقترن بمثل العامل في المبدل منه لقصد التأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r5.claim: Alternatively, the statement may coordinate with “he strove,” meaning Pharaoh ordered it proclaimed throughout his kingdom, beyond the crowd gathered by his palace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة : فقال أنا ربكم } عطفا على جملة { يسعى } على أن يكون فرعون أمر بهذا القول في أنحاء مملكته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r6.claim: He called himself the highest lord either as Amun-Ra’s son and successor in that status, or because Pharaoh was then regarded as lord of the many gods, making “highest” an explanatory epithet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p80/r6.anchor: فوصف نفسه بالرب الأعلى لأنه ابن ( أمون رع ) وهوالرب الأعلى ، فابنه هو القائم بوصفه ، أو لأنه كان في عصر اعتقاده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r2.claim: Pharaoh gathered the people of his kingdom and called out that he was their highest lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r2.anchor: وقوله فحشر معناه: جمع أهل مملكته ثم ناداهم بقوله: أنا ربكم الأعلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse’s sequence means he called first, then gathered the people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: المعنى: فنادى فحشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r4.claim: Pharaoh’s claim to be the highest lord exemplifies extreme fabrication that persisted among Egypt’s kings and followers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433/r4.anchor: نهاية في المخرقة ونحوها باق في ملوك مصر وأتباعهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r1.claim: Pharaoh's claim means that no lord exists above him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r1.anchor: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى أي لا رب فوقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r2.speaker: unattributed view
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r2.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes Pharaoh to mean that idols are gods, with him as their lord and the people's lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r2.anchor: وقيل أراد أن الأصنام أرباب وأنا ربها وربكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r3.speaker: unattributed view
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r3.claim: Another unnamed interpretation takes him to mean that he is lord of the masters and leaders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p21#4/r3.anchor: وقيل أراد أنا رب السادة والقادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r3.claim: They say Pharaoh made this claim forty years after saying that he knew no god for his people but himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: وهذه الكلمة قالها فرعون بعد قوله: {ما علمت لكم من إله غيري} [القصص: 38] بأربعين سنة

MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God seized Pharaoh for both claims: first that he knew no god for his people except himself, then that he was their highest lord.
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ﴿ فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى ﴾ يقول أخذه الله بكلمتيه كلتيهما أما كلمته الأولى قوله ﴿ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ﴾ وأما الآخرة

MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation as Ibn Abbas for Pharaoh's punishment for his two claims.
MUJAHID:v2p727#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد مثله

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r13.claim: Moses offered Pharaoh continued kingship, youth without aging, and Paradise after death if he confessed God as Lord and himself as God's servant; Pharaoh replied that a man is worshiped as lord only if he has a lord.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r13.anchor: لك ملكك فلا يزول، ولك شبابك فلا تهرم، ولك الجنة إذا مت، على أن تقول ربي الله وأنا عبده، فقال فرعون: إنك لعاجز بيننا يكون الرجل ربا يعبد حتى يكون له رب،

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r14.claim: By calling himself the highest lord, Pharaoh claimed that no lord was above him.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r14.anchor: فقال، فرعون: { أنا ربكم الأعلى } يقول: ليس لي رب فوق، فذلك الأعلى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh claimed that no lord stood above him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى ﴾ لا رب فوقى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#2/r2.claim: His people nevertheless had idols that they worshipped.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r9.claim: His boast means that no lord is above him.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r9.anchor: { أنا ربكم الأعلى } أي لا رب لكم فوقي.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r10.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r10.claim: Al-Tha'labi recounts that Iblis appeared to Pharaoh as a man in an Egyptian bath; when Pharaoh failed to recognize him, Iblis asked how he could, since Pharaoh claimed to have created him, then repeated Pharaoh's boast.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r10.anchor: فقال له إبليس: ويحك! أما تعرفني؟ قال: لا. قال: وكيف وأنت خلقتني؟ ألست القائل أنا ربكم الأعلى. ذكره الثعلبي

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r11.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r11.claim: He says Pharaoh made small idols for his people and meant that he was lord over their idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r11.anchor: وقال عطاء: كان صنع لهم أصناما صغارا وأمرهم بعبادتها، فقال أنا رب أصنامكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r12.claim: One interpretation says Pharaoh was lord of the leaders and chiefs, who in turn were lords over the lower people.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r12.anchor: وقيل: أراد القادة والسادة، هو ربهم، وأولئك هم أرباب السفلة.

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r1.claim: Pharaoh gathered the magicians as in al-Shuara, then proclaimed his claim at their gathering, sent an announcer to proclaim it, or addressed the people himself.
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r1.anchor: فحشر فجمع السحرة كقوله : { فأرسل فرعون فى المدائن حاشرين }

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's first claim was that he knew no god for the people besides himself, and his final one was that he was their highest lord.

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r3.claim: Razi rejects the literal idea that Pharaoh believed himself creator of the cosmos, since its falsity is self-evident; one who doubts this is insane, and God would not send prophets to an insane person.
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r3.anchor: لا يجوز أن يعتقد الإنسان في نفسه كونه خالقا للسموات والأرض والجبال والنبات والحيوان والإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r4.claim: Razi says Pharaoh was a materialist denying a Creator and resurrection, claiming only he could command or forbid; ربكم meant your nurturer and benefactor, since he denied any deity or messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r4.anchor: بل الرجل كان دهريا منكرا للصانع والحشر والنشر

RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r5.claim: Al-Qadi says that after the staff became a serpent and exposed Pharaoh's helplessness, his claim to be the highest lord was incongruous; he seemed deranged and unaware of his words.
RAZI-FULL:v31p39#3/r5.anchor: قال القاضي : وقد كان الأليق به بعد ظهور خزيه عند انقلاب العصا حية

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r16.speaker: R, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r16.claim: Several reports say Pharaoh first claimed that he knew no god for his people other than himself, then proclaimed himself their highest lord.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r16.anchor: Pharaoh first said, O notables! I know of no god for you other than myself (28:38), then I am your lord most high

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r4.claim: Pharaoh claims divinity and, on the apparent meaning, ranks himself above the other gods acknowledged by his polytheistic people.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r4.anchor: وظاهره أنه يدعي أنه أعلى في الربوبية من سائر الأرباب التي كان يقول بها قومه الوثنيون

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r5.claim: He may have meant that he was the most proximate deity, controlling people's provisions and affairs and preserving their honor, unlike the other gods.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r5.anchor: أنه أقرب الآلهة منهم تجري بيده أرزاقهم وتصلح بأمره شؤون حياتهم ويحفظ بمشيئته شرفهم وسؤددهم

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r6.claim: Another view reads the boast as political supremacy over officials and governors, effectively a claim to kingship, like his boast about Egypt's kingdom.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r6.anchor: وقيل مراده بما قال تفضيل نفسه على كل من يلي أمورهم ومحصله دعوى الملك

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r7.claim: The political reading conflicts with the apparent wording and Pharaoh's explicit claims that no god exists for his people besides him.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r7.anchor: وهو خلاف ظاهر الكلام وفيما قال قوله لملإه يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

TABRISI:79:15-24/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r22.claim: Pharaoh's boast means that he claimed there was no lord above him.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r22.anchor: { فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى } أي لا رب فوقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r1.claim: Muqātil says Pharaoh stood on his throne when the people assembled and proclaimed himself their supreme lord, claiming no lord stood above them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r1.anchor: لما اجتمعوا قام عدو الله فرعون على سريره. {فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى} أي لا رب فوقكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Pharaoh had made small idols for the people and told them to worship them, claiming to be lord of both them and their idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p188#5/r2.anchor: كان قد صنع لهم أصناما صغارا، فقال لهم: اعبدوها وأنا ربكم ورب أصنامكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r5.claim: His claim that he was the highest lord means he believed no lord was above him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:20-25/r5.anchor: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى } ليس رب فوقي.

TABRISI:79:25-26/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r9.claim: Pharaoh’s claim to be the only one who can harm others and cannot be harmed is false; this is an attribute of God, creator of Pharaoh and all creatures.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r9.anchor: وكذب واللعين إنما هذه صفة الله الذي خلقه وخلق جميع الخلائق

TABRISI:79:25-26/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r10.claim: Another view says Pharaoh made idols his lords and claimed to be both their lord and his people’s.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنه جعل الأصنام أربابا فقال أنا ربها وربكم

BURHAN:v2p60/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p60/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p60/r5.claim: The claim that Pharaoh says “your gods” yet “I am your highest lord” can be reconciled if the gods were considered his property and he worshipped them in his people’s religion before inviting them to rank him highest.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r1.claim: The poem's address appears to be the Prophet but indirectly refers to his family; its critics and reproachers are the Umayyads.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r1.anchor: فالخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمراد أهل بيته، فورى عن ذكرهم به، وأراد بالعائبين واللائمين بني أمية

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r2.claim: The lines cannot be aimed at the Prophet himself: no Muslim would reproach someone for praising him, and no one equals or surpasses him.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r2.anchor: وليس يجوز أن يكون هذا للنبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم، لأنه ليس أحد من المسلمين يسوءه مدح رسول الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r3.claim: Poets exaggerate praise even for ordinary men without attracting blame; therefore restraint in praising the Prophet is no grounds for reproach.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r3.anchor: وإن الشعراء ليمدحون الرجل من أوساط الناس فيفرطون ويفرطون فيغلون وما يرفع الناس إليهم العيون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls Pharaoh’s claim the height of fabrication and says its like persisted among Egypt’s kings and followers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r14.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قول فرعون ذلك نهاية في المخرقة، ونحوها باق في ملوك مصر وأتباعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r15.claim: Abū Ḥayyān attributes Egyptian royal deification to Ismaili rulers, beginning with al-Muʿizz and ending when Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn removed the doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r15.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك لأن ملك مصر في زمانه كان إسماعيليا، وهو مذهب يعتقدون فيه إلهية ملوكهم

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.claim: Pharaoh's punishment answered his later claim “I am your highest lord” and his earlier claim “I know no god for you but myself.”
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.claim: Abū Bakr says the two boasts were forty years apart, attributing the account to Ibn ʿAbbās through Abū Ḥuṣayn and Abū al-Ḍuḥā.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر، وسئل عن هذا، فقال: كان بينهما أربعون سنة

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the first boast as Pharaoh's claim to be the only god and the later one as his claim to be the highest lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the two boasts and reports a forty-year interval between them.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى}

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī gives the same identification of Pharaoh's two boasts as retribution for the first and later claims.

TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.claim: ʿĀmir likewise identifies the two boasts as Pharaoh's claims to divinity and to being the highest lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p84/r6.anchor: عن زكريا، عن عامر، {نكال الآخرة والأولى}

THALABI:v10p127/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r3.claim: One explanation of Pharaoh's claim is that there is no lord above him.
THALABI:v10p127/r3.anchor: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى يقول ليس رب فوقي

THALABI:v10p127/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r4.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p127/r4.claim: Another explanation is that Pharaoh meant the idols were lords, while he was lord of the idols and of the people.
THALABI:v10p127/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد أن الأصنام أرباب وأنا ربها وربكم
